name: GlzSidebar
semanticRole: Provide persistent secondary navigation and organization for hierarchical workspace content, with optional search, grouping, favorites, badges, resizing, and compact transformation.

material.rule: Desktop sidebars are solid by default and normally 220–320px wide. Under constrained layouts the sidebar compresses or transforms to an overlay or sheet; persistent dense navigation does not default to blur.

input.keyboard: Supports sequential or tree-style navigation appropriate to hierarchy, group disclosure, search, item activation, and keyboard-accessible resize and collapse controls.
input.focus: Focus identifies the current sidebar item or control independently from selected destination.
input.hover: Hover may reveal row actions and resize affordance without making them pointer-only.
input.press: Press feedback is immediate on items and collapse or resize controls.
input.selection: Selected item uses subtle accent tint, filled or active icon where appropriate, and semibold label.
input.directManipulation: Resizable variants use a visible divider with a forgiving hit region and persist width only at the documented logical scope.

accessibility.role: Use navigation or complementary landmark semantics plus the appropriate nested list or tree pattern for the actual hierarchy.
accessibility.name: The sidebar landmark and ambiguous icon controls expose stable programmatic names.
accessibility.state: Current destination, expansion, collapse, disabled, loading, error, and resize state are exposed when applicable.
accessibility.value: Resizable width may be exposed through an accessible separator when user-adjustable; navigation items do not invent synthetic values.
accessibility.keyboard: All navigation, disclosure, search, collapse, and resizing operations have keyboard equivalents.
accessibility.focus: Focus is always visible and remains distinct from the selected destination.
accessibility.errorAssociation: Sidebar search/load errors are associated with the affected region and include recovery text.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Collapse and overlay transformation becomes direct or a short glide/crossfade.
accessibility.reducedTransparency: Overlay or exceptional Glaze variants resolve to opaque surfaces.
accessibility.increasedContrast: Strengthen selected, focus, group, and resize boundaries.
accessibility.forcedColors: Use system colors and explicit current/expanded/focus states.
accessibility.largeText: Items and groups reflow while the workspace remains reachable and horizontal overflow is contained.

fallbacks.reducedMotion: Use direct or short collapse and overlay transitions.
fallbacks.reducedTransparency: Use opaque sidebar or overlay surfaces.
fallbacks.highContrast: Strengthen selection, focus, grouping, and resize affordances.
fallbacks.forcedColors: Use platform colors and explicit structural states.
fallbacks.performance: Remove blur and decorative shadow before altering hierarchy or persistence.

content.overflow: Sidebar contents scroll internally; labels truncate only when full names remain accessible. Sidebar width must not force workspace-level horizontal overflow.
content.localization: Group labels, item names, badges, search text, and actions tolerate expansion; uppercase group labels are generally avoided.
content.rtl: Sidebar placement, indentation, disclosure, resize edge, and leading/trailing actions mirror semantically.

criteria: Desktop width remains within the intended 220–320px range unless product-specific evidence justifies otherwise.
Selected destination is clear without turning every row into a pill.
Compact and touch row densities preserve appropriate effective hit targets.
Constrained transformation to overlay or sheet preserves information architecture and selected context.
